headline_en: 84 Bangladeshis nominated for Japanese scholarship
summary_en: The Ministry of Education announced that 84 Bangladeshis were nominated for Japan's MEXT scholarship 2024-25 across research, undergraduate, college of technology and specialized training college levels. Nomination does not guarantee the scholarship; the Japanese embassy will hold written and oral exams and the Japanese authority decides. The article also explains what MEXT is.

facts.statement: 84 Bangladeshis were nominated for the Japanese government's MEXT scholarship 2024-25: 16 for research PhD, 20 for research master's, 30 for undergraduate, 8 for specialized training college and 10 for college of technology programmes.

For the MEXT scholarship 2024-25, nomination by Bangladesh's Ministry of Education does not guarantee the scholarship; the Embassy of Japan holds written and oral exams and the relevant Japanese government authority decides on award based on the results.
The list of Bangladeshis nominated for Japan's MEXT scholarship 2024-25 was published on the Ministry of Education's website.

MEXT (Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology) scholarship is given by the Japanese government to students from about 160 countries since 1954 and is described as the most prestigious Japanese government scholarship.
A visa obtained for the Japanese MEXT scholarship carries the words 'Govt. Scholar'.

headline_en: Australia will keep duty- and quota-free access for Bangladeshi goods after middle-income graduation: foreign minister
summary_en: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong met Bangladesh Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud in Dhaka on Tuesday 21 May 2024. Topics included export of skilled manpower from Bangladesh, seasonal employment of Bangladeshis, welfare of Bangladeshis in Australia, preventing irregular migration and TAFE support for Bangladesh's technical training centres. Australia will keep duty- and quota-free access for Bangladeshi goods.

facts.statement: At a meeting in Dhaka on 21 May 2024, Bangladesh Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud and Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong discussed export of skilled manpower from Bangladesh, seasonal employment for Bangladeshis, welfare of Bangladeshi expatriates in Australia and preventing irregular migration. No agreement on these was reported.
facts.source_in_article: Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud at joint press briefing

facts.statement: Bangladesh's foreign minister said on 21 May 2024 he asked Australia for advanced training support for Bangladesh's Technical Training Centres under Australia's Technical and Further Education (TAFE) assistance.

Premier University in Chittagong has a credit transfer arrangement with the Australian university UTC (as printed); on 21 May 2024 the two foreign ministers discussed whether this could be extended to other Bangladeshi universities.
Bangladesh-Australia trade rose to 4 billion Australian dollars over the last four years, and Bangladesh hopes it will double in the next five years.

headline_en: Ambassador in Uzbekistan going to Bishkek to look after Bangladeshis
summary_en: After local mobs attacked foreigners, including Bangladeshi students, in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan from 16 May 2024, Bangladesh sent its ambassador in Uzbekistan to Bishkek. Bangladesh has no embassy in Kyrgyzstan; the Tashkent embassy covers it. Some students asked to be brought home by charter flight.

facts.statement: From the night of 16 May 2024 local people in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan attacked foreigners, including Bangladeshi, Pakistani and Indian students, going house to house beating foreigners and vandalising, and entering medical college hostels; there were also allegations of abuse of foreign women students. It followed a 13 May clash between two or three locals and some Egyptian medical university students.

Bangladesh's foreign ministry said on 19 May 2024 that the situation in Bishkek had improved since the night of Saturday 18 May; Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud said there was no report of any Bangladeshi student being badly injured and that Bangladesh had conveyed its concern to the Kyrgyz government.
facts.source_in_article: Foreign ministry statement; Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud

facts.statement: Bangladesh has no embassy in Kyrgyzstan; the Bangladesh embassy in Uzbekistan is responsible for Kyrgyzstan.

On 19 May 2024 Bangladesh's ambassador to Uzbekistan, Mohammad Monirul Islam, said he was trying to go to Kyrgyzstan quickly to meet its foreign and home ministries, and that the embassy was in contact with the students.

Some Bangladeshi students in Kyrgyzstan asked to be returned to Bangladesh by charter flight in May 2024; the ambassador in Uzbekistan said this would be conveyed to the proper authority. No decision was reported.
Several hundred Bangladeshi students, among other Bangladeshis, were in fear in Kyrgyzstan in May 2024.

Bangladesh's ambassador to Austria in April 2024 was Asad Alam Siam; Bangladesh has an embassy and permanent mission in Vienna.

headline_en: Money sweeter than honey vs when money is more poisonous than poison
summary_en: An opinion column on rising millionaire numbers and loan defaults alongside debt-driven suicides and crimes in Bangladesh. It cites a housewife in Munshiganj who borrowed 12-14 lakh taka from six NGOs and individuals to send her husband abroad and killed herself and her two children under the repayment pressure on 26 February 2024. It also mentions young people drowning in the Mediterranean.

facts.statement: Salma Begum, a housewife in Sirajdikhan upazila, Munshiganj, had borrowed 12-14 lakh taka from six NGOs and several individuals to send her husband abroad; on 26 February 2024, under pressure to repay, she made her two children drink poison and hanged herself.
A Prothom Alo columnist wrote in April 2024 that while millionaire numbers rise in Bangladesh, many young Bangladeshis are drowning in the Mediterranean Sea.

headline_en: 10 foreign languages that will give you an edge in building a better career
summary_en: A careers feature lists ten foreign languages useful for careers (Mandarin, Japanese, German, Turkish, Spanish, Korean, French, Arabic, Italian, Russian) and says where each can be learnt in Bangladesh, mostly the Institute of Modern Languages at Dhaka University. It notes Korean can be learnt at the Bangladesh Korea Technical Training Centre and Arabic at the Islamic Foundation.

facts.statement: The Institute of Modern Languages at Dhaka University teaches Mandarin Chinese, Japanese, German, Turkish, Spanish (part-time and long-term), Korean, French, Arabic, Italian and Russian; some private institutions also teach Chinese.
Korean can be learnt in Bangladesh at the Institute of Modern Languages, Dhaka University and at the Bangladesh Korea Technical Training Centre.

Arabic, described as essential for workers in the oil industry, energy sector and high-end construction in the Middle East, can be learnt in Bangladesh at the Islamic Foundation and the Institute of Modern Languages, Dhaka University.
German can be learnt in Bangladesh at the Institute of Modern Languages, Dhaka University and at Goethe-Institut Bangladesh, which is recognised by the German embassy.
French can be learnt at Dhaka University's Institute of Modern Languages and Alliance Française; Russian at the Institute of Modern Languages and the Russian Centre of Science and Culture.
The article says Japanese language skill along with industry skills is given priority for jobs in research and development, manufacturing and engineering, and logistics in Japan.

headline_en: The same group destroyed the banking sector and is crashing the share market
summary_en: Interview with economist Mustafa K Mujeri on banking, share market, prices and reserves. On remittances he says growth is held back by the controlled exchange rate, which makes hundi profitable; most workers who went abroad in the last two to three years are labourers who went on loans and must send money, but it is not coming through legal channels. He adds most Bangladeshi migrant workers are unskilled.

facts.statement: Economist Mustafa K Mujeri said in April 2024 that remittance growth is held back by the exchange rate: remittances come both through legal channels and illegally through hundi, and if sending via hundi is more profitable, money will come that way; a market-based exchange rate would greatly increase legal inflows.
facts.source_in_article: Mustafa K Mujeri, Executive Director, Institute for Inclusive Finance and Development (InM)

facts.statement: Mustafa K Mujeri said in April 2024 that most Bangladeshis who went abroad in the previous two to three years are workers, most of whom went on loans and must repay them while also sending money to families; they are sending money but not through legal channels.
Mustafa K Mujeri said in April 2024 that legal options to send remittances have expanded, through banks and digital channels, and that most Bangladeshi migrant workers are unskilled.

headline_en: Bangladeshi women in UK and France suffer after being trolled on TikTok
summary_en: Based on a BBC investigation, Bangladeshi women living in the UK say they have been trolled, harassed and threatened on TikTok, allegedly by Hasan Sayed, a Bangladeshi living in a Paris suburb. Police complaints and platform reports achieved little. One victim's husband, Kamrul Islam, got help via the UK embassy in Paris to file a complaint with the Paris prosecutor, and the UK Information Commissioner's Office told TikTok, YouTube and Facebook to remove videos within seven days.

facts.statement: Several Bangladeshi women in the UK told the BBC that Hasan Sayed (হাসান সায়েদ), a Bangladeshi living in a Paris suburb with thousands of TikTok followers, collected their personal photos and information from social media, put them in troll videos, mocked them in TikTok lives and threatened rape and murder; he did not respond to the BBC's emails and calls.

In February 2023 Kamrul Islam, a Bangladeshi living in Staffordshire, UK, contacted the UK embassy in Paris, which connected him to English-speaking French lawyer Matthieu Croizet (ম্যাথিউ ক্রোইজেত); the lawyer filed a complaint at the Paris public prosecutor's office alleging at least three offences by Hasan Sayed under French law, including violent threats, threats to rape a child and an adult, child pornography and cyberbullying. Case status was unknown and the lawyer said it would take a long time.
facts.source_in_article: Kamrul Islam and lawyer Matthieu Croizet via BBC

facts.statement: In April 2023 Kamrul Islam complained to the UK Information Commissioner's Office, which found the videos concerning and, citing misuse of children's personal data, told TikTok, YouTube and Facebook to remove the videos within seven days; the three platforms said content breaching their community guidelines would be removed and the accounts blocked.

Bangladeshi women victims of TikTok trolling in the UK and France said complaints to police and to the platforms often produced no effective action; TikTok told Kamrul Islam the videos did not breach its community guidelines and police offered no hope.
Lawyer Matthieu Croizet told the BBC that Islamophobia is strong in France and the complaint could stall because the complainant's surname contains 'Islam'.

headline_en: US offering fellowships to Bangladeshi teachers
summary_en: The American Center of the US Embassy in Dhaka was taking applications for the Fulbright Teaching Excellence and Achievement (TEA) programme, a six-week exchange in the US for secondary school teachers in January or September 2025. The article lists benefits including J-1 visa support, eligibility rules, documents and English test requirements.

facts.statement: The Fulbright Teaching Excellence and Achievement (TEA) programme, run by Washington DC-based nonprofit IREX with sponsorship from the US State Department's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs and advertised by the American Center of the US Embassy in Dhaka, is a six-week exchange in the US for Bangladeshi secondary school teachers, held in January or September (spring or autumn) 2025, including a two-week internship at a US secondary school.
The application deadline for the Fulbright TEA fellowship is printed as Saturday 30 March 2025 (as printed in a March 2024 article); finalists are usually informed by the end of September.

Fulbright TEA benefits include J-1 visa support, a pre-departure orientation in Dhaka, round-trip and domestic US airfare, a welcome orientation in Washington DC, programme fees, accommodation (usually shared) and meals, accident and health insurance, travel to the internship school if needed, a book/professional development allowance, a closing seminar, hosting a US teacher for two weeks, and eligibility to apply for post-programme grants.

Fulbright TEA applicants must be current full-time secondary teachers of English, EFL, maths, science, foreign languages, social studies, journalism/communication or special education; hold a bachelor's degree; have at least five years of full-time teaching; have excellent English; know Microsoft Office, Word and Excel; be Bangladeshi citizens living in Bangladesh; hold a valid Bangladeshi passport; and apply online.
Ministry of Education officials, education administrators, full-time teacher trainers, university teachers and private English tutors are not eligible for Fulbright TEA.

Fulbright TEA applicants must submit an Institutional Support and Reference Form (ISRF) completed by a supervisor, a Leave Approval Form (LAF) from https://fulbright.irex.org/, a copy of passport information pages and undergraduate/postgraduate transcripts uploaded in 'Section XV. Supplemental Documents'.

Shortlisted Fulbright TEA candidates must take TOEFL or IELTS, needing a paper-based IELTS score of 6.0 or above or equivalent; candidates with a valid score need not retake; the American Center arranges the tests; shortlisted candidates are interviewed in English.
Fulbright TEA forms and online application: https://fulbright.irex.org/

headline_en: Long gap no problem: chance to do BA and BSS while living abroad
summary_en: Bangladesh Open University's SSHL school opened admission for its 2024 batch of the Outside Bangladesh (NISH-2) BA and BSS programmes for Bangladeshi migrants or people of Bangladeshi origin in Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Italy, South Korea and the UAE, through the Bangladesh embassy in each country. The article gives the deadline (30 March 2024), eligibility, documents, fees by year (USD 250, 190, 220), process, online classes on weekly holidays and contacts.

facts.statement: Bangladesh Open University (BOU) SSHL school runs an Outside Bangladesh (NISH-2) BA and BSS programme for Bangladeshi migrants or people of Bangladeshi origin working or living in Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Italy, South Korea and the UAE, with admission through the Bangladesh embassy in each country; admission for the 2024 batch ran until 30 March 2024 with classes starting April 2024.
The BOU NISH-2 BA/BSS programme lasts 3 years and 6 semesters of 6 months each; registration stays valid for up to 5 academic years.

To join the BOU NISH-2 BA/BSS, the applicant must have passed HSC/Alim/A-level or equivalent and be a Bangladeshi citizen migrant, or of Bangladeshi origin, in Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, UAE, Italy or South Korea.

Documents needed for the BOU NISH-2 online application: scanned recent photo (300x300 pixel), signature (300x100 pixel), SSC and HSC (or equivalent) certificates and mark sheets, national ID/smart card/birth registration certificate, passport, residence permit card, and proof of admission fee payment.
BOU NISH-2 BA/BSS fees: first year USD 250 (semester 1: 135 + semester 2: 115), second year USD 190 (100 + 90), third year USD 220 (95 + 125); each year's fee is paid at admission to that year.

To apply to BOU NISH-2, pay USD 250 for the first and second semester as instructed on the website or Facebook page of the Bangladesh embassy in the country, fill in the online form, then download and print it and submit it with documents and fee proof to that Bangladesh embassy.

In BOU NISH-2, exams for semesters 1-2, 3-4 and 5-6 are held together in years one, two and three; online tutorial classes (eight per course) and exams are held on the host country's weekly holiday, so students need a device with internet; e-books are used mainly, and free printed books can be obtained by contacting IAPW.

BOU NISH-2 contacts: Bangladesh embassy in Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Italy, South Korea or UAE; Dean, SSHL School, BOU: bousshl2019@bou.ac.bd; International Academic Program Wing (IAPW), BOU: iapw@bou.ac.bd; websites iapw.bou.ac.bd or bou.ac.bd; e-books at ebookbou.edu.bd/ba_bss.php.
